_note: One entry per step. 'asks' come from docs/requirements.md. 'api' is the function(s) the step must define so the scorer can call it. AGREE THESE WITH T7 BEFORE RUNNING.

asks: Out of all our past batches, show me the handful that were truly exceptional.
Give me a quick picture of a normal batch from our cellar: what each lab reading usually looks like.
api: remember(rows) -> list of rows: the exceptional batches, at most 5% of the data rows
summary(rows) -> dict mapping each column name to its typical value

asks: Before the panel sits, estimate what score this new batch will get from its lab sheet alone.
Group our batches into a few kinds, and tell me what score to expect from each kind.
api: guess(train, row) -> float: predicted Quality+ for one batch, using only the train rows
kinds(train) -> list of (group_rows, expected_quality) pairs

asks: When you say batch A will beat batch B, tell me whether that's a real difference or just tasting noise.
How often are your score estimates right on batches you've never seen before?
api: certify(train, a, b) -> 'A', 'B' or 'same': which batch will score better, or 'same' if the difference is just noise
accuracy(train, test) -> float: share of test batches whose guessed score rounds to the true Quality+

asks: As each new batch comes off the line, tell me right away whether it's worth sending to the panel.
Keep sharpening your sense of what makes a good batch as this season's scores come in, without starting over.
api: start(names) -> model: an empty model that knows only the header row NAMES
learn(model, row) -> model: the model after seeing one more scored batch (ROW includes its goals); must not refit from scratch
predict(model, row) -> float: predicted Quality+ for one batch, from what the model has seen so far
worth(model, row) -> bool: True if this batch looks worth sending to the panel (predicted Quality+ of 6 or more)

asks: The panel can only taste 20 batches this month. Which 20 should they taste to find our best wine?
Find me a batch that scores high but stays low in alcohol, while tasting as few batches as possible.
api: In this step the goal cells (Alcohol-, Quality+) of every data row are '?' until tasted. label(row) -> the same batch with its goals filled in; each call is one tasting.
taste(rows, label, budget=20) -> list of labelled rows: the batches it chose to taste, in the order tasted; calls label at most BUDGET times
choose(rows, label, budget=20) -> row: the best batch found (high Quality+, low Alcohol-), tasting at most BUDGET batches

asks: Our low-scoring batches: which lab readings are dragging them down?
Which two or three readings matter most for whether a batch scores well?
api: blame(train, k=3) -> list of K lab-reading column names (never a goal column): the readings that matter most for Quality+, most important first
dragging(train) -> list of (column name, 'high' or 'low') pairs: readings that are too high or too low in poor batches (Quality+ below 6), worst first

asks: This batch was flagged as poor. Explain why in words my cellar staff will understand.
If a buyer asks why we rated this batch premium, give me a short reason I can defend.
api: verdict(train, row) -> 'good' or 'poor': 'good' if the batch's predicted Quality+ is 6 or more
why(train, row) -> list of (column name, '<' or '>=', number) conditions: every one holds for ROW, and train batches meeting all of them mostly share ROW's verdict
explain(train, row) -> str: the verdict and its reason, in one or two plain-English sentences

asks: This batch is heading for a poor score. What's the smallest change to its chemistry that would lift it?
If we can only adjust sulphates and acidity, how should we change them to move this batch up a grade?
api: fix(train, row, only=None) -> dict mapping lab-reading column names to new values: the smallest change predicted to raise ROW's Quality+; if ONLY is a list of column names, change only those (never goal columns)

asks: Flag any lab sheet that looks wrong: a typo, a broken sensor, a reading that doesn't fit.
Warn me when a batch is unlike anything we've made before, so I don't trust a prediction for it.
api: odd(train, row) -> bool: True if this lab sheet looks wrong (a typo, a broken sensor, a reading that doesn't fit)
novel(train, row) -> bool: True if this batch is unlike any batch in TRAIN

asks: Are your picks for the panel any better than just tasting batches at random?
How does your scoring stack up against a standard off-the-shelf model?
api: vs_random(rows, label, budget=20) -> 'better', 'same' or 'worse': are this trial's choose() picks better than BUDGET random tastings? Run both several times and decide with a statistical test, not a single comparison.

vs_baseline(train, test) -> 'better', 'same' or 'worse': is this trial's guess() more accurate on TEST than always predicting the mean Quality+ of TRAIN? Decide with a statistical test on the per-batch errors.
